material_defect.issue: Remote artifact collection rejects symlinks and realpath escapes but does not reject hardlinked files (st_nlink > 1). A declared file can therefore be a hardlink to bytes also reachable through an undeclared or future-split path. pathlib.resolve() remains the declared pathname, so the realpath guard accepts it. GNU tar archives a lone hardlinked declared file as a regular file when its sibling path is not also in the archive, so the local tar member hardlink guard does not detect the alias.
material_defect.impact: Violates exact artifact allowlist/future-split fail-closed durability contract. A success-path bundle can contain bytes aliased from undeclared or future-split storage without either remote path validation or local tar validation detecting the alias.
material_defect.required_repair: Before hashing or archiving every declared file and every file recursively discovered under a declared directory, require stat().st_nlink == 1 (or an equivalently strict inode-ownership rule proven to reject external aliases). Add deterministic regression tests where a declared file is hardlinked to an undeclared/future-split file and require fail-closed rejection before bundle creation. Preserve all existing 14 tests, exact declared roots, hashes, remote execution semantics, and science bytes. Fresh independent review required after freeze.
